observed_coverage_gaps: HTML dashboard output quality and interaction are not represented in the legacy output rubric.
Scores 1, 2, and 4 have no behavioral anchors.
An aggregate score can conceal an unacceptable readability, visibility, trustworthiness, or executive-suitability dimension.
No negative-control or metamorphic case proves that a plausible-looking but unsupported output fails.
The stated 0.80 quality threshold conflicts with the legacy 76/90 pass threshold.
Legacy and sprint baseline scores use a /50 denominator without a reproducible receipt under the current 90-point rubric.

preserve_legacy_critical_gates: PDF and PowerPoint share the same evidence hash
both rendered report artifacts pass semantic QA

proposed_changes.change: Evaluate report and HTML outputs through separate route-conditioned gates while preserving all legacy PDF/PPTX trust gates.
proposed_changes.expected_impact: Adds real HTML coverage without allowing an irrelevant artifact to raise another route's score.
proposed_changes.risk: A route can be misclassified or a required artifact can be omitted from its gate.
proposed_changes.regression_gate: Analytics-report cases must still require synchronized valid PDF/PPTX artifacts; HTML cases must require a self-contained valid dashboard, deterministic QA receipt, usable filters, nonblank visuals, and no PDF/PPTX creation.

proposed_changes.change: Score readability, visibility, trustworthiness, and executive suitability separately and require a minimum score in every required dimension in addition to the weighted overall threshold.
proposed_changes.expected_impact: Prevents score inflation from compensating for a critical weak dimension.
proposed_changes.risk: Poorly calibrated floors can create false failures at category boundaries.
proposed_changes.regression_gate: Each dimension must publish evidence-backed diagnostics; trustworthiness cannot be compensated by presentation scores; threshold changes require a versioned rationale and comparison receipt.

proposed_changes.change: Replace undefined intermediate scores with observable anchors and require every nonbinary score to cite artifact evidence and a deterministic check or named human-review observation.
proposed_changes.expected_impact: Reduces ambiguous ratings, score drift, and unreviewable high scores.
proposed_changes.risk: Overly prescriptive anchors may miss valid novel presentations.
proposed_changes.regression_gate: A score without criterion ID, evidence locator, observation, and rater/check provenance must fail closed; qualitative exceptions must be explicit and cannot bypass hard gates.

proposed_changes.change: Add held-out negative controls for unsupported claims, broken evidence hashes, blank or clipped visuals, secret leakage, wrong-route artifacts, and plausible but unrelated charts; add order/whitespace/path metamorphic checks.
proposed_changes.expected_impact: Detects benchmark gaming, false positives, path sensitivity, and nondeterminism.
proposed_changes.risk: Fixture leakage or brittle textual assertions can make controls easy to game or flaky.
proposed_changes.regression_gate: Held-out expected results remain immutable to optimizers; repeated deterministic runs must agree; assertions target structured receipts and artifact semantics rather than exact prose.

proposed_changes.change: Remove unreceipted baseline claims from acceptance decisions and emit both machine-readable JSON and an executive Markdown summary with denominator, coverage, skipped cases, hard-gate state, and score delta.
proposed_changes.expected_impact: Makes benchmark progress auditable and understandable without reading test logs.
proposed_changes.risk: Summaries can diverge from the canonical receipt.
proposed_changes.regression_gate: Markdown values must be derived from and cross-checked against one canonical JSON receipt; missing, skipped, or unexecuted cases cannot count as passes.

accept_only_if: Workflow evaluator reports no loss of feature or agent coverage.
All legacy trust hard gates remain fail-closed.
HTML output coverage is present and route-isolated.
At least one held-out negative control catches a plausible false positive.
Repeated deterministic runs produce identical status and scores.
